entities.summary:
Abu-Shama al-Maqdissí was an Arab historian who chronicled the history of the Crusaders and the Kingdom of Jerusalem. Born in the 12th century, he traveled extensively throughout the Mediterranean, gathering information and insights that would shape the understanding of the period. His work, 'The History of the Crusaders', remains a valuable source for historians and scholars today.

Abū Shāma Shihāb al-Dīn al-Maḳdisī's significance lies in his ability to provide a nuanced and detailed account of the events and figures of the Crusader era. His work offers a unique perspective on the complexities of medieval politics and society, making him a crucial figure in the study of the period.

The legacy of Abū Shāma al-Maqdissí can be seen in the continued study and analysis of his work. His contributions to the field of Crusader studies have ensured that his work remains relevant and influential to this day.

Abū Shāma al-Maqdissí's 'History of the Crusaders' contains a striking statistic: the estimated number of deaths during the Crusades was over 1 million people, making it one of the deadliest conflicts in human history.

Abū Shāma Shihāb al-Dīn al-Maḳdisī was an Arab historian born on January 17, 1203, in Damascus, Syria, and died on June 19, 1267. He is considered one of the most important Arab historians of the medieval period, known for his detailed chronicles of the Middle East and his analysis of the Crusades. His works, such as 'The History of the Crusades' and 'The History of the Sultans', provide valuable insights into the politics, society, and culture of the region during this time.

Al-Maḳdisī's writings were heavily influenced by the works of Ibn Khaldun, a Tunisian historian and Islamic scholar. He also drew upon the knowledge of Greek historians such as Polybius and Diodorus Siculus, as well as Arabic sources like the Muḥammad ibn Ibrāḥīm al-Muqaffa's works.

One of the most significant contributions of Al-Maḳdisī was his portrayal of the Crusades as a complex and multifaceted phenomenon. He argued that the Crusades were driven by a combination of religious, political, and economic factors, and that they had far-reaching consequences for the Middle East and Europe.

Al-Maḳdisī's work had a profound impact on the development of historiography in the Islamic world. His emphasis on the importance of primary sources and his attention to detail helped to establish a new standard for historical writing.

The legacy of Al-Maḳdisī can be seen in the works of later historians, such as Ibn Battuta and Sultān Shihāb al-Dīn Ahmad al-Tanjī. His writings also continue to be studied by scholars today, providing valuable insights into the history of the Middle East during the medieval period.

Al-Maḳdisī's writings are characterized by their erudition and scholarship. His use of multiple sources and his ability to synthesize complex information into a coherent narrative make him one of the most important historians of the medieval period.
